 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
 Court Of Small Causes, At Bengaluru.

 Xxiii Additional Small Causes Judge, Bengaluru.

 S/o Late Manjaiah,

 Advocate.)
2 SCCH-25 MVC 2797/2022  JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 06.04.2022.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:

sentences.text: On 06.04.2022 at about 08.00pm, the petitioner was standing on the footpath on the Road near NH-75, B.M.Road, Nuggehalli Cross, Hirisave Town, Channarayapattana Taluk, Hassan District.

At that time the Driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 13-F-2273 suddenly came from Hassan with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed against the Petitioner.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to the both bone right leg.
Immediately he was shifted to Govt. Hospital at Hirisave wherein he was given first aid treatment.
Later he was shifted to HIMS Hospital, Hassan wherein he was admitted as an inpatient from 07.04.2022 to 11.04.2022, surgery was done and discharged with advice.
So far he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards hospital, medical expenses, food and nourishment, conveyances, attendant charges and other incidental charges.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, the injuries are not yet healed and the petitioner has suffered from permanent disability.
Prior to the date of accident the petitioner was working as an Agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries he is not able to work as prior to the date of accident.
The accident occurred due to the negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2273.

The Jurisdictional Hirisave Police have registered a case in Cr.NO.47/2022 p/u/Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC against the driver of the said KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2273 and later filed charge sheet.
The Respondent being the RC owner and internal Insurer of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-13-F-2273 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.

5. The Objection of the Respondent is as; It has denied the averments made in the petition and stated that the Bus was assigned on the schedule from Dharmasthala to Bengaluru, driven by its driver A.Nagesh, Token No.799 and it was proceeding from Dharmasthala To Bangalore by observing all the traffic Rules.
The driver of the Bus has completed the schedule trip without any type of accident.
There was no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus and the petitioner has fallen on his own and has filed false case against the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

1 . Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 06.04.2022 at about 8.00pm due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2273 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or Award?

sentences.text: 2 7. The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.
Mr. Jagadish - Record Technician at HIMS Govt. Hospital, Hassan got examined as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.9 to P.12.
On the other side, the Respondent examined Mr.Nagesh - Driver of the KSRTC Bus as RW.1 and did not produce any documents on their side.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
9.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: In the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-

In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-13-F-2273, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments in his chief examination affidavit and produced 7 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.7.
During his cross-examination he has stated that there was a Zebra crossing at the spot.
That he does not drink Alcohol.
He is an illiterate.
He has stated that the complainant is his brother's son who has a Tea Shop near the accident spot.
He has also admitted that there were no street lights at the spot.
He got examined the MRO of HIMS Hospital as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.9 to 12 i.e., authorization letter, case sheet, MLC register extract and X-rays.
During his cross-examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The Respondent has contended that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
In order to prove the same, the respondent has got examined its Driver as RW.1, who has reiterated the objections in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination he has admitted that the charge sheet is filed against him and he has not challenged the same.
11. On perusal of Ex.P.1 it is clear that the accident occurred on 06.04.2022 at 08.00pm and the FIR was registered on the next day of the accident on the complaint of relative of the petitioner.
The Mahazar at Ex.P.2 was conducted on 07.04.2022 which mentions that the complainant has a Tea shop right in front of the accident spot.
The Sketch at Ex.P.3 shows the accident spot very near to the divider and very far from the left side of the Road.
PW.1 has stated that he was standing on the footpath.
Therefore, there is no clarity as to how the accident spot could be on the extreme right side of the Road.
The police have seized the bus as per Ex.P.4 seizure mahazar.
As per Ex.P.5 the IMV report the Bus has suffered damage to the front right bumper scratched which also shows that the petitioner was standing on the right side of the Road.
The Wound Certificate at Ex.P.6 shows that the petitioner has suffered injuries in the RTA dated 06.04.2022.
After thorough investigation, the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the KSRTC Bus at Ex.P.7.

On perusal of all these Shivanna vs K.S.R.T.C on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120948238/
3 documents

it appears that the petitioner has gone to the extreme right side of the Road and waiting near the divider to cross the road, during that time the KSRTC Bus came on the same way in a rash and negligent manner and without observing the petitioner has hit him.
Moreover, it was the duty of the driver of the KSRTC Bus to see if anybody was standing near the divider and he should not have driven the bus in high speed.
Therefore, this Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the Driver of the KSRTC Bus.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-

The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accidental injury he is suffering from open segmental fracture both bones right leg which are grievous injuries, since the injuries have caused permanent disability.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.6 discloses that, he has sustained grievous and simple injury.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/- under the head of Pain and Suffering.
The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
In this regard he has not produced any medical bills to prove the treatment expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at HIMS Govt. Hospital, Hassan and treated as an inpatient.
During that time, certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.95,000/-.

13. LIABILITY:
As discussed above the Respondent has failed to prove its defence about the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.95,000/- along with interest @
6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.

14. Issue No.3:-

4 For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.95,000/- (Rupees  Ninety Five Thousand only) along with  interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent being the RC  owner of the offending vehicle shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through e- payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
